title: Differentiable Physical Optimization
problem: Gate sizing and buffer insertion are interdependent VLSI physical optimization tasks typically solved in decoupled manner, yielding suboptimal results; existing simultaneous methods use oversimplified timing models or heuristics, lacking mathematical rigor.
motivation: High-performance circuit design requires unified optimization of interdependent physical design tasks for better timing closure.
method: Presents a differentiable physical optimization framework with GPU acceleration integrating gate sizing and buffer insertion: timing-aware buffer tree skeleton construction, physics-aware modeling, and discrete-aware optimization algorithms.
key_novelty: First differentiable framework mathematically unifying gate sizing and buffer insertion with rigorous physical modeling.
contributions: Differentiable physical optimization framework for gate sizing and buffer insertion
23% TNS improvement, 12% WNS improvement with 30× speedup versus CPU flow

metrics.ppa: 23% TNS improvement, 12% WNS improvement with similar power

limitations: Evaluation on specific benchmark circuits; applicability to very large designs or specialized cell types not discussed.
